chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Rifah ibn Musa said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man divorced his wife with a single divorce, so she became fully divorced from him. Then another man married her, and he divorced her according to the Sunnah (one divorce), so she became fully divorced from him. Then the first man married her again. How many divorces does she have with him? He said: 'With no count (i.e., one divorce is sufficient).' Then he said: O Rifah, what if he divorced her three times, then she married a second man, and that second man received the divorce (i.e., gave her one divorce)? If he divorced her once, she would have two (divorces remaining).

key_terms.اسْتَقْبَلَ الطَّلَاقَ: received the divorce (i.e., initiated the divorce from his side)
key_terms.عَلَى السُّنَّةِ: according to the Sunnah (referring to a single, revocable divorce)
key_terms.عَلَى غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ: with no count (meaning one marriage is sufficient)
key_terms.فَتَبِينُ: she becomes fully divorced (free to marry others)

ai.seo_question: How many divorces are required for a woman to return to her first husband after a triple divorce if the intermediate marriage ends with a single divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the mechanics of *Talaq al-Mughallazah* (the major divorce), specifically addressing the scenario where an intermediate husband divorces his wife with a single, revocable divorce (*Talaq Raj'i*) before the *Iddah* expires. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains that this single divorce counts as one of the required three, meaning the first husband can remarry her with a new contract, as the cycle is effectively reduced to two remaining divorces. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the intermediate marriage being a genuine, consummated union (*Nikah Mufawwid*) rather than a mere formality, ensuring the woman’s transition between husbands is legally and spiritually valid.
